title: Freemium is a marketing strategy, not pricing: why bootstrappers should usually avoid it
summary: Rob Walling argues freemium is really a lead-generation marketing strategy, and that bootstrapped SaaS founders copying VC-funded giants risk delaying revenue and burning resources. He lays out four conditions that must all be present before freemium makes sense, and suggests a 10x price increase as an alternative thought experiment.

principles.text: Freemium is a marketing strategy, not a pricing strategy, because the price is zero and it exists to fill the funnel with leads.
principles.quote: realistically premium is a way for you to get more leads into your funnel and that's why it is much more of a marketing strategy than pricing

principles.text: Don't copy freemium from VC-funded giants; bootstrappers lack the funding and know-how for when and how to implement it.
principles.quote: those companies have hundreds of employees tens of millions if not hundreds of millions of dollars raised many of them are actually public now you don't have that

principles.text: Freemium pushes revenue down the line, which is dangerous when a bootstrapper needs to hit $5K-10K a month to quit their job.
principles.quote: do you have the time to wait 12 months to get 3% of your free users to give you revenue or do you need to force those who are willing to pay to pay you sooner

principles.text: A free plan doesn't market itself, and you need very large user volumes to convert enough paying customers.
principles.quote: just having a free plan isn't enough you also then have to Market it it doesn't Market itself

principles.text: Freemium needs four ingredients: near-zero support, near-zero incremental cost, self-onboarding with fast value, and virality.
principles.quote: having almost zero support for each customer having almost zero incremental cost for additional users so if they're sending AI requests to to an API or if they're sending SMS messages this doesn't work

principles.text: Instead of adding a free plan, ask what you'd have to build to justify a 10x price and move upmarket.
principles.quote: what would it be like as a thought experiment to go the opposite direction not have a free plan but to 10x your pricing instead to increase prices to try to lower turn and go up market
